data.title: NVIDIA Faces Ransomware Threat, but Breach Claims Remain Unverified
data.description:
A 10-Day Countdown Raises Questions

NVIDIA has been listed on the dark-web extortion website of ransomware group The Gentlemen, which is threatening to release allegedly stolen data within approximately 10 days. The listing, posted on 18 November, includes a countdown timer and a contact channel for ransom negotiations.

However, the group has yet to publish any evidence of the alleged breach. No sample files, data inventory, or technical details identifying the affected systems or business units have been provided. The listing alone does not establish that NVIDIA's internal network has been compromised.

NVIDIA Investigates a Possible Third-Party Incident

NVIDIA said it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner. The company stated that it has found no indication its own systems or networks were affected and that it continues to monitor the situation.

The statement leaves open the possibility that the incident could involve a supplier, contractor, or external partner rather than NVIDIA's core infrastructure. The relationship between the third-party investigation and The Gentlemen's extortion claim has not yet been conclusively established.

Why Researchers Are Urging Caution

Cybersecurity researchers have cautioned against accepting ransomware claims at face value. The Gentlemen has previously been accused of exaggerating attack claims, misattributing stolen information to organisations, or reusing previously exposed data.

Without verifiable samples, investigators cannot determine the authenticity, origin, sensitivity, or volume of the alleged stolen information. Even if data eventually emerges, further investigation would be required to confirm whether it originated from NVIDIA, a partner, or another source.

The group reportedly operates a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) model, allowing affiliates to carry out attacks using its tools and infrastructure. Such leak-site listings are commonly used to pressure organisations into negotiations, regardless of whether the full extent of an intrusion has been established.

The Wider Risk of Third-Party Exposure

The incident highlights a persistent cybersecurity challenge: organisations can face data exposure through their wider supply chain, even when their own systems remain uncompromised.

Partners, cloud providers, contractors and software vendors may have access to business information, credentials or operational systems. A security weakness within one of these external environments can potentially create risks for multiple organisations.

Companies should therefore review third-party access privileges, monitor data-sharing arrangements, enforce strong authentication, and ensure that vendors meet cybersecurity and incident-reporting requirements.

Conclusion: A Threat Is Not Proof of a Breach

The NVIDIA case remains an evolving cybersecurity incident, with the ransomware group's allegations yet to be substantiated. The countdown may be intended to increase pressure on the company, but it is not evidence that sensitive information has been stolen.

Until verified data or further official findings emerge, organisations and the public should distinguish between ransomware claims and confirmed security incidents. The case also serves as a reminder that cybersecurity resilience extends beyond an organisation's internal network to every partner and service provider connected to its operations.

data.title: South Korea to Ban Private Lenders From Offering General Personal Loans to Soldiers After Borrowing Jumps 69 Times in Three Years
data.description:
From Barracks Bunks to Borrowed Millions: Why Korea Is Curbing Loans to Soldiers

A corporal posted a request on an online platform that links borrowers with private moneylenders last November.

He was due to leave the army the following June and already owed about 20 million won ($15,000) to banks, savings banks and other lenders.

His question was short:

"Is there anywhere I could get my hands on 5 million won?"

His plea is now a regular sight on such sites, and South Korea's financial regulator has decided to act.

The Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) intends to bar private lenders from offering general-purpose personal loans to active-duty servicemen.

🇰🇷 JUST IN: South Korea plans to restrict high-interest loans to active-duty soldiers after borrowings hit ₩24.2B (~$17M), linked to crypto and online gambling.

— CryptoMeter.io (@CryptoMeterIO) November 15, 2026

How Did Lending to Soldiers Grow So Fast?

The numbers show how quickly the market expanded.

According to the Financial Services Commission, the 30 largest registered loan companies lent 24.2 billion won ($17.5 million) to active-duty servicemen in 2025.

That compares with 350 million won ($254,000) in 2022, a rise of almost 69 times in three years.

Regulators link the jump to easier access to online betting and speculative investment.

Soldiers have been allowed to use smartphones after duty hours since 2020, which has put gambling sites within reach of the barracks.

Higher pay has added to the mix.

A sergeant's monthly compensation has more than doubled, from 676,100 won ($490) in 2022 to 1.5 million won ($1,090) this year.

군대 간 아들 있는 집은 이거 한 번 보셈
병장 월급이 두 배 되는 동안 병사 대출은 69배 뛰었음

1. 상위 30개 대부업체 현역병 대출: 2022년 말 3억5천만원 → 작년 말 242억원
2. 병장 월급은 67만6천원 → 올해 150만원
3. 은행·저축은행은 현역병 신용대출 안 해줌. 근데 일부 대부업체가… pic.twitter.com/nfA2rLCtMY

— 펌질하는고닉 (@PJG0012e) November 18, 2026

Why Can Private Lenders Reach Soldiers That Banks Cannot?

Mainstream lenders such as banks and savings banks generally refuse unsecured personal loans to serving soldiers, who cannot provide the usual income documents.

Private lenders have filled the gap by accepting copies of military pay account statements as proof of income.

That practice is the target of the new rule.

The proposal was discussed on 12 November at the fifth meeting of the Financial Consumer Protection Advisory Committee, chaired by FSS Governor Lee Chan-jin, and the regulator confirmed it on 15 November.

The FSS has agreed with the Korea Consumer Loan Finance Association to add the ban to the industry's standard operating guidelines by the end of the year.

Enforcement will rely on industry self-regulation, and the FSS will work with the Financial Services Commission and the banking sector to finalise the details.

Not every loan will be blocked.

Collateralised loans and small emergency cash loans will remain available, as the authorities accept that soldiers may need money quickly for living costs.

병장 월급이 두 배 되는 동안 병사 대출은 69배 뛰었음

1. 상위 30개 대부업체 현역병 대출: 2022년 말 3억5천만원 → 작년 말 242억원
2. 병장 월급은 67만6천원 → 올해 150만원
3. 은행·저축은행은 현역병 신용대출 안 해줌. 근데 일부 대부업체가… pic.twitter.com/nfA2rLCtMY

— 펌질하는고닉 (@PJG0012e) November 18, 2026

How Big Is the Gambling Problem in the Army?

The full extent is hard to measure, but Army figures give some indication.

Military police booked 1,721 servicemen on suspicion of online gambling between 2021 and 2025.

That is a small share of an army of more than 320,000 personnel, yet soldiers say betting is far more common among their peers than the official count suggests.

What Do Debt Relief Applications Show?

Requests for help point to growing strain.

The number of active-duty personnel seeking support from the Credit Counseling & Recovery Service stayed in the 400s each year from 2019 to 2021.

It then rose to 753 in 2022 and 1,015 the following year.

A further 322 had applied by April this year, which puts the annual total on course to approach 1,000.

The size of the debts has grown as well.

Average borrowing among servicemen seeking restructuring was 34.01 million won ($24,700) in 2019 and passed 50 million won ($36,300) in 2022.

It reached 58.63 million won ($42,600) as of April this year.

Is This Only a Military Problem?

Experts caution against treating it as one.

Yang Jun-seok, a professor of economics at the Catholic University of Korea, said,

"Debt among servicemen should be understood as part of the broader problem of mounting debt among young people, rather than as an issue unique to the military. Young people are increasingly exposed to financial risks as they take a more active interest in high-risk assets such as cryptocurrencies."

What Else Is the FSS Planning?

Alongside the lending limits, the FSS plans to widen financial education across the armed forces.

That includes more one-on-one counselling and programmes that warn of the dangers of online gambling and leveraged investing.

Starting today, victims of illegal lending in Korea can apply for help online instead of going to a center in person.

Applications are open 24/7 on the Credit Counseling & Recovery Service website or app. Until now, you had to visit one of 22 offices nationwide.

Once you apply,…

— James Kim (@King_James_Kim) November 15, 2026

The regulator also announced wider flexible operations for bank branches and a shorter notification cycle for long-unused prepaid electronic payment accounts, cut from one year to three months.

data.title: ‘Doomed From the Start’: President Trump’s Meme Coin Hits New Lows After Midterms
data.description:
President Donald Trump's official TRUMP meme coin is facing mounting pressure after plunging to a new all-time low following the US midterm elections, with analysts warning that fading investor interest, potential congressional scrutiny and a substantial token unlock schedule could leave the cryptocurrency struggling to recover.

Now that US can investigate the President as an illegal scammer Here’s a list of tokens launched by Trump and his circle: World Liberty Financial (WLFI token) – Token sale raised $550M (Oct 2024 – Jan 2025) – Trump-linked entity holds 22.5% of supply – Tokens held by founders valued at $3.8B USD1 Stablecoin (World Liberty Financial) – Market cap reached $5B – Backed by US treasuries and cash – Estimated interest revenue $135M per year TRUMP Memecoin – Launched Jan 2025 – Insider cash-outs estimated at ~$800M – Token price later collapsed 95% MELANIA Memecoin – Launched Jan 2025 – Reached ATH $13 – Later collapsed ~98% Trump Digital Trading Cards (NFTs Series 1–4) – Initial sales revenue ~$9–10M+ – Licensing fees reported: $7.15M – Ongoing secondary royalties Trump “Mugshot” NFT Edition – $1M in secondary market volume – Generates continuous royalty income DJT Token Program (Trump Media) – Announced Jan 2026 – Tokens distributed to DJT shareholders – Partnered with Crypto com Estimated crypto money generated or attributed to Trump and his circle so far: ~$1.4B realized cash & revenue ~$3.8B+ in unrealized token value This is the largest personal crypto ecosystems ever built by a political figure. Max extraction and without justice (yet)

— StarPlatinum (@StarPlatinum_) November 4, 2026

The token has fallen nearly 40% since election day, briefly touching $0.896 over the weekend. While TRUMP has staged a modest rebound, analysts believe its problems extend beyond the latest political developments, pointing to its speculative nature and lack of sustainable demand as major obstacles to a meaningful recovery.

TRUMP Meme Coin Plunges as Political Pressure Mounts

TRUMP touched $0.896 over the weekend, marking its lowest price since launching in January 2025. The token subsequently rebounded approximately 8% to $0.965, but remained nearly 40% below its election-day price and 98.7% below its all-time high of $73.43, reached the day after its launch.

Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares revealed that the midterm elections had added pressure to an already struggling token. Trading volume increased around the vote, suggesting that some investors had positioned themselves for a potential Republican victory.

An investor put $3.19 MILLION into Donald Trump's memecoin 1 year ago. Today it's worth $258,000. @grok how much have all $TRUMP holders lost in total, and is it the worst-performing coin ever launched by a president? https://t.co/200cpb5GDi

— CryptoReviewing (@CryptoReviewing) November 18, 2026

However, the election results triggered what Nolan described as a “visible unwind,” contributing to a sharp sell-off as those positions were reversed.

The political fallout could create further challenges for Trump's cryptocurrency ventures. Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, claimed that Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress in January and potentially using their subpoena powers to investigate Trump's crypto businesses, which could ultimately negatively affect Trump-affiliated assets.

“Democrats take both chambers in January and plan to use their subpoena power on his crypto ventures. His net approval rating has almost never been lower."

President Donald Trump told "60 Minutes" this week he knew “nothing” about the World Liberty Financial crypto company that helped him take in more than $2 billion last year alone. Democrats who’ll take control of Congress in January have big plans to find out more. The incoming heads of various oversight committees are already naming a broad array of investigative targets regarding Trump’s personal and administrative actions. They’re demanding records, promising subpoenas – and warning people and companies not to destroy any documents. 📸: SAUL LOEB/Pool via REUTERS Read more: https://t.co/zIAugNuRm3

— USA TODAY (@USATODAY) November 15, 2026

Other Trump-linked investments have also struggled since the election. World Liberty Financial's WLFI token has declined 7.5%, while shares of Trump Media & Technology Group have fallen 32%, according to Decrypt data.

Trump's cryptocurrency ventures have also attracted political scrutiny surrounding the Clarity Act, legislation intended to establish a formal regulatory framework for much of the cryptocurrency industry. Democrats raised concerns about the Trump family's involvement in crypto businesses, which reportedly generated more than $1 billion in a year.

Fading Demand and Token Unlocks Raise Further Concerns

Beyond political uncertainty, analysts argue that TRUMP faces a more fundamental problem: its limited ability to generate lasting demand.

Shannon described the token as having “no value accrual,” arguing that it has increasingly lost momentum as public interest in the project fades. Google Trends data also shows searches for $TRUMP have remained largely flat since June 2025.

“Right now, if you Google the word ‘idiot’… a picture of Donald Trump comes up. How would that happen?” Google CEO Sundar Pichai faces questions from Congress over Google Search. https://t.co/YeuRL6jUBf

— Channel 4 News (@Channel4News) December 11, 2018

Nolan similarly characterized the token's appeal as “largely speculative,” noting that holding TRUMP does not provide investors with a clear connection to the success of an underlying business.

One of the token's most prominent incentives, exclusive dinners for major holders, has also struggled to maintain interest. Ahead of the third gala, 130 wallets appeared on the final leaderboard, holding a combined $8.6 billion worth of TRUMP. That figure represented a 94% decline compared with the holdings associated with the first dinner.

As the top holder of $TRUMP and proud supporter of President Trump, it was an honor to attend the Trump Gala Dinner by @GetTrumpMemes. Thank you @POTUS for your unwavering support of our industry! #MakeCryptoGreatAgain🇺🇸 https://t.co/Yy2TuWEgzT

— H.E. Justin Sun 👨‍🚀 🌞 (@justinsuntron) May 23, 2025

The token's supply structure presents another challenge. According to Nolan, the majority of TRUMP tokens were allocated to Trump-linked entities and are being gradually unlocked, meaning demand must continue growing to absorb the additional supply entering the market.

For a meme coin whose appeal depends heavily on attention surrounding a single individual, maintaining that level of demand could prove difficult.

Analysts Question Whether TRUMP Can Ever Recover

The combination of declining investor enthusiasm, political uncertainty and future token unlocks has raised questions about whether TRUMP can regain its previous market highs.

Nolan believes Trump's eventual departure from office could accelerate the token's gradual decline, as its appeal remains closely tied to his political influence and public visibility. He also warned that major Trump-related headlines could trigger temporary price rallies without necessarily establishing sustainable demand.

You can’t make this sh*t up. A Trump supporter lost nearly $33K on Trump tokens and somehow blames Democrats and “anti-Trump investors,” not Trump, who made $1.5 billion from his crypto scam in 2025. It’s a cult. https://t.co/w3uejY5Cuz

— Republicans against Trump (@RpsAgainstTrump) July 2, 2026

Shannon, however, believes the token could continue losing value even while Trump remains politically influential. He described a recovery to its previous highs as “incredibly unlikely,” noting that the price would need to increase approximately 82-fold to reach its former peak.

“I think the meme coin was doomed from the start, and like with most meme coins, creating long-term demand is a Sisyphean task.”

For TRUMP, the challenge is no longer simply recovering from its latest post-election sell-off. The token must also overcome declining public interest, limited utility and a substantial amount of supply still waiting to unlock, leaving its long-term prospects increasingly uncertain.

data.title: Druckenmiller Interview: Daring Not to Go Long or Short, Aiming to Break Even
data.description: Legendary investor Stan Druckenmiller publicly stated that he has almost completely liquidated his equity positions, entering "capital preservation mode"—a rare proactive exit in his 50-year investment career. On November 18, 2026, Druckenmiller spoke with Iliana Bouzali, head of global derivatives at Morgan Stanley, at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. He bluntly stated that today's macroeconomic environment is "completely reversed" compared to January of this year: the Federal Reserve has shifted from rate cuts to rate hikes, commodities have reversed their upward trend, credit spreads continue to widen, and market visibility is unprecedented in his career. "I can't recall a time when I was so lacking in judgment about the direction of the next 12 months," he said. Just nine months ago, Druckenmiller was heavily bullish within the same framework—long on stocks, long on copper, short on US Treasuries, and betting on a healthcare turnaround. Now, that portfolio is almost wiped out. Describing his current position, he says: "Equity longs and shorts are roughly balanced, I hold a small dollar position, and I'm shorting copper. Overall, we're in capital preservation mode." His phone's automatic reply reportedly consists of only a few words: "Don't talk to me. I'm not playing." He also revealed that he believes the next big opportunity in the AI ​​field lies in "selling tasks" rather than "selling computing power"—once top AI labs master the world's most powerful intelligence, they can completely bypass the token pricing model and directly enter vertical sectors such as cybersecurity and healthcare, building their own commercial empire. The bullish logic of January has completely collapsed. Druckenmiller's assessment in January was based on a comprehensive macroeconomic framework: a federal funds rate of 3.5%, a nominal growth rate of 6%, indicating extremely loose monetary policy; the Fed's dot plot suggesting further rate cuts this year; commodity prices such as copper breaking new highs; market up/down lines continuously reaching new highs; and credit spreads extremely narrowing. "With such excessively loose monetary policy, a recession within 6 to 12 months seems almost impossible to me," he said. At that time, he was optimistic about the acceleration of AI capital expenditure, going long on stocks, long on copper, and shorting US Treasuries as a hedge, and was also bullish on the healthcare sector. However, about a month later, the "US tariffs" event disrupted his strategy. He admitted that there was panic selling at the time, but he quickly bought back in, and in the process, he naturally purified his positions—those without significant upside potential were cleared out, while the logic behind his AI infrastructure-related positions became clearer. By November, he listed each condition that initially supported his bullish judgment, pointing out that they had all reversed: the Federal Reserve stopped cutting interest rates and instead raised them; he mentioned someone who had worked with him for 15 years, who was deeply dissatisfied with the zero-interest-rate policy of the past 15 years and even more dissatisfied with inflation exceeding the target for five consecutive years, suggesting a fundamental shift in the Federal Reserve's internal policy orientation. Commodities have peaked and are now falling back after breaking new highs; he is currently shorting copper. The stock market's up-and-down line peaked as early as August 14th, although the index peaked in October. Credit spreads continue to widen. "You should understand what I mean. Everything is completely reversed from back then," he said. "I'm out!" A proactive exit during a moment of uncertainty. Faced with this situation, Druckenmiller chose to exit. His equity positions are roughly balanced after offsetting long and short positions, holding a small dollar position, and he is generally in a wait-and-see state. Bouzali jokingly remarked that he had set up an "auto-reply" button in his Zoom calls with only one message: "Don't talk to me. I'm not playing." He didn't deny it. He explained that this proactive withdrawal wasn't an admission of defeat, but rather a reflection of his consistent risk management logic. His investment framework spans four major asset classes: commodities, bonds, stocks, and interest rates, which means he never needs to maintain continuous exposure to any single class. "Bonds and currencies tend to perform the best during stock market bear markets," he said, making him more inclined to remain inactive in stocks and instead look for opportunities in other macroeconomic instruments. He also admitted that he doesn't use VaR or conduct stress tests; the core signal for risk management is whether the P&L itself performs as expected. “When the market is in chaos and enters a bear market, all correlations break down,” he said. “Some very talented people have painfully proven this this year when they were shorting software and going long on AI infrastructure.” He also discussed his belief in “winning and losing streaks”—he believes that investment cycles far exceed random distributions, and identifying whether one is currently in a “hot” or “cold” state is one of the most important parts of the job. “When I’m in a good state, I go all in; when I’m in a bad state, I only make small bets, waiting for the average cost to recover before deciding whether to increase my position again.” He characterized his current situation as a “rest,” which could last two days or six months. From Selling Shovels to Selling Services: The Second Half of AI? Despite overall position reduction, Druckenmiller's long-term judgment on AI remains unwavering. He explicitly stated that he will not short-sell innovations in this field, partly because related stocks are already oversold and positions have been cleared. His judgment on the next stage of AI focuses on "use cases" rather than "infrastructure." He believes that there may be tactical trading opportunities in the AI ​​infrastructure sector, but it will no longer be the main engine as it has been in the past four years. The real opportunity, he believes, lies in the top AI labs themselves. His logic is that a lab possessing the world's most advanced AI has no reason to remain stuck with a token-based business model. "If you have the world's most powerful AI, you can start selling tasks instead of tokens; you can build your own business," he says. He specifically cites cybersecurity as the most direct example: "Who can compete with these people in cybersecurity? They created these problems, so now they can protect us with swarms of intelligent agents." Healthcare is also within his purview. He summarized this judgment in one sentence: "Sell tasks, not tokens." Fiscal Risks and Educational Concerns: Slow-Moving Variables When asked about important trends that are currently "quietly unfolding," Druckenmiller raised two structural issues he has long been concerned with. One is the continued decline of K-12 basic education in the United States. He pointed out that the United States has long compensated for this shortcoming by attracting top overseas talent. "I bet eight of the top ten tech companies were founded or led by immigrants." But he worries that tightening immigration policies are threatening this compensatory mechanism, and the two problems combined have not yet attracted sufficient policy attention. Secondly, there's the issue of fiscal policy. Back in 2011-2012, he traveled to various universities, trying to persuade young people to pay attention to intergenerational fiscal inequality, but almost no one paid attention. He quoted the old saying: "How does bankruptcy happen? First slowly, then suddenly." He believes that the United States will likely experience a fiscal reform forced by the financial market crisis within the next 10 years, "which will be a crisis completely different from the current one." He also expressed cautious optimism that the reform will eventually occur. 10-Year Predictions: Nuclear Fusion, Space Data Centers, and Cancer Conqueror Druckenmiller also gave three 10-year predictions, each accompanied by what he considered a reasonable probability: Nuclear Fusion: A 20% probability of it happening within 10 years, or at least a clear indication that "we are about to achieve it." Space Data Centers: Speaking in Austin, he gave it a "at least 70%" probability. Conquering Cancer: He spent 30 years on the board of directors of Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, witnessing the iterations from gene sequencing and immunotherapy to AI. "I think we will conquer cancer. I think it will become a manageable disease. I'm talking about within 10 years, not 20." What Makes a Top Investor? At the end of the conversation, Druckenmiller shared his judgment on the qualities of an investor. He believes the difference between top investors and excellent investors lies in four points: an almost pathological passion for the business, an extremely strong thirst for knowledge, a "pathological" level of competitiveness, and strict self-discipline. “Every time you buy, there’s a seller on the other side, and if you don’t put in an amazing amount of work, you’ll lose in this industry,” he said. He also discussed a common pitfall for highly intelligent people: loving their arguments so much that they forget the second part of the saying, “Don’t put all your eggs in one basket and watch that basket.” “They can have great arguments, they can make great bets, but things change, and they just can’t adjust as quickly as others.” He also mentioned his most painful lesson: in January 2000, he sold his Nasdaq shares but bought them back on the same day the market peaked. “I think I missed the top by less than an hour.” When asked what he learned from this, he replied, “Nothing. I knew I shouldn’t have done it, but I just couldn’t control myself.”

data.title: Anthropic IPO priced at $83; employees may be poised for a wealth feast.
data.description:
Author: Joanne, Tencent Technology

Anthropic's IPO price ultimately exceeded the previously set upper limit.

On November 18th, US time, Anthropic officially announced that it had set its IPO price at $83 per share, higher than the previously announced range of $70 to $78. Based on a fully diluted valuation, the company's valuation is approaching $1.5 trillion.

Previously, Anthropic's IPO order book had already approached $500 billion. Faced with demand far exceeding the offering size, the company also considered increasing the number of shares issued, ultimately pushing the offering price up to $83. The impact of this IPO extends beyond how much money Anthropic raised. For the public market, it will become an important benchmark for observing the valuation of AI companies. For the company's thousands of employees, this could also be a staggering cash-out. Nearly $500 billion in subscription intentions pushed up the offering price. Anthropic initially planned to issue 825 million shares at a price of $70 to $78 per share, raising approximately $64.4 billion based on the upper limit of the offering range. However, during the roadshow, investor demand rapidly increased. According to sources, when Anthropic closed its order book, institutional investors expressed subscription intentions of approximately $400 billion, and individual investors demanded nearly $100 billion, totaling close to $500 billion. The final offering price of $83 was approximately 6.4% higher than the previously announced upper limit of $78. Previous reports also indicated that Anthropic was considering expanding its IPO to respond to market demand. This has made Anthropic's IPO one of the most watched deals in global capital markets this year. In comparison, SpaceX raised approximately $85.7 billion in its June IPO, setting a record at the time. Anthropic's IPO has not only attracted huge subscription interest but has also prompted the market to compare the valuations and employee wealth effects of the two companies. From $83 to $282: The Potential Valuation of Anthropic

Based on a static, fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion, if the stock price rises to $90, the company's valuation will approach $1.63 trillion, similar to Meta's current market capitalization; at $104, the valuation will be approximately $1.88 trillion, approaching TSMC; at $190, the valuation will reach approximately $3.43 trillion, close to Google; and at $282, the valuation could exceed $5 trillion, approaching Apple's.

These figures are not stock price targets, but simple calculations based on current valuation and share capital. As the company's share capital, market price, and the market capitalization of other tech giants change, these comparison points will also adjust accordingly.

But this at least illustrates one point: above its $83 IPO price, Anthropic has entered the valuation competition range of the world's largest tech companies. Investors are no longer just buying into a rapidly growing AI startup, but rather betting on its potential to become a global tech giant. Thousands of employees may become millionaires, with early employees benefiting the most. Another major winner of this IPO may be Anthropic's own employees. Public data shows that as of September 30, Anthropic employees held approximately $119 billion in stock options with a weighted average exercise price of only $2.91 per share. Of these, approximately $73 billion in options have already vested, and employees can exercise them according to relevant arrangements. Options granted earlier had even lower costs. Documents show that options granted in 2023 that are still unexercised have an average exercise price of only $0.52. Based on the IPO price of $83, the book value of these early-stage shares has seen a dramatic increase. Two private equity market research firms also estimated the potential wealth of employees. Sacra estimates that approximately 2,800 current and former Anthropic employees may possess at least $1 million in vested equity. Hill's estimate suggests that the equity of 598 non-founding employees could be worth over $100 million. These figures are models built based on publicly available information, not the individual employee shareholding figures disclosed by the company. Actual returns will also need to consider vesting schedules, exercise costs, and taxes. It's worth noting that this wealth feast isn't just for engineers and researchers. A 2024 administrative job posting reviewed by Reuters shows an annual salary of $140,000 to $190,000, explicitly listing equity as a significant component of total compensation. This means that some early-joining administrative and support staff may also benefit from equity appreciation. Anthropic's workforce is also rapidly expanding. As of the end of September this year, the company had approximately 5,300 employees, compared to only about 940 by the end of 2024. For early employees, holding low-cost stock options may be the biggest reward from this IPO. However, paper wealth is not the same as cash that can be immediately converted. According to the listing arrangements, non-founding employees can sell up to 10% of their shares on the first trading day, and are subject to further restrictions on subsequent sales. Interestingly, just days before the IPO pricing, Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei had a public live-streamed dialogue with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon. When discussing the company's IPO and valuation, Amodi mentioned that he consulted many people during the IPO preparation process, and one piece of advice particularly impressed him: never let a company's valuation exceed its actual worth by even a single dollar. He also linked this principle to Anthropic's long-standing business philosophy—underpromise and overdeliver. Today, institutional investors' nearly $500 billion in subscription intentions have pushed Anthropic's offering price to $83, valuing it close to $1.5 trillion. Amodi's emphasis on restraint stands in stark contrast to the enthusiasm shown by the capital markets. Anthropic stock is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on November 19th (US time), under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering price has been set; the market will now provide further answers through actual trading: whether investors are willing to continue buying at higher prices, and whether this AI company can support such a large valuation with its future performance.

data.title: Coinbase Brings ChatGPT Into Crypto Trading As Binance Expands Its AI Ambitions
data.description:
Coinbase and Binance-linked crypto projects are positioning themselves for an emerging battle over AI-powered financial services, as cryptocurrency platforms look to integrate artificial intelligence into trading and decentralized finance.

Coinbase is bringing cryptocurrency trading directly into ChatGPT, allowing eligible users to manage portfolios and execute trades through conversational instructions. Meanwhile, PancakeSwap has rebranded as Pancake, reflecting its expansion beyond decentralized token swapping as the BNB Chain ecosystem develops its own AI-powered infrastructure.

The developments highlight two different approaches to the emerging agentic economy, with Coinbase focusing on bringing AI-powered financial services directly to consumers while Binance expands the infrastructure available to developers and autonomous agents.

Coinbase Brings Crypto Trading Directly Into ChatGPT

Coinbase's new ChatGPT integration allows eligible users to connect their accounts, check balances, analyze portfolio holdings and trade cryptocurrencies and equities without leaving the AI chatbot.

Users can request market or limit orders through everyday language, with ChatGPT displaying an interactive confirmation card containing the transaction details before execution. Every order requires explicit user approval before Coinbase processes it through its Advanced Trade platform.

The launch also builds on Coinbase's existing AI infrastructure through its Coinbase for Agents toolkit, which provides developers with connections to trading accounts and market data. By bringing these capabilities into ChatGPT, Coinbase is extending its AI-powered services beyond developer tools and into a more accessible consumer interface.

Pancake Expands Beyond DeFi Swaps as Binance Builds AI Infrastructure

Beyond its expanding DeFi services, Pancake is also exploring the potential of AI-powered autonomous agents. Coinbase and Binance Compete for the Future of AI-Powered Finance

The latest developments reveal two different strategies emerging in the competition for AI-powered financial services.

Coinbase is focusing on the consumer experience by bringing trading capabilities directly into ChatGPT, allowing users to interact with their portfolios and place orders through conversational instructions. Rather than competing solely for human traders, Coinbase and Binance are positioning their respective ecosystems to support a future in which AI-powered applications and autonomous agents play a larger role in trading, portfolio management and decentralized finance.

data.title: What market challenges does Bitcoin currently face?
data.description:
While Bitcoin rebounded somewhat after its weekend plunge, its overall performance was not strong. More noteworthy than price is the fact that the market pressures have not disappeared.

Rising expectations of a Fed rate hike, volatile tech stocks, and changes in the global financing environment are all influencing investor sentiment towards Bitcoin.

Firstly, the Fed's stance: the minutes of its October meeting released last night were clearly hawkish, with almost all officials believing that further rate hikes would still be necessary.

Previously, CME FedWatch showed that market expectations for a 25 basis point rate hike in December had risen to 95%.

Behind this is persistent inflationary pressure.

US import prices rose 1.5% month-on-month in October, the largest increase since monthly records began, while industrial output fell 0.4% during the same period. Economic activity has slowed, but import prices, such as equipment, are rising, making it difficult for the Federal Reserve to easily shift to an easing stance. For Bitcoin, high interest rates not only mean increased financing costs but also reduce the willingness to hold high-risk assets. Previously, the market expected interest rate cuts to improve liquidity, but this expectation is now being dashed. The outlook for tech stocks is also not optimistic. The AI ​​investment boom continues, but the market is beginning to focus on whether the huge capital investment will bring corresponding returns. The Fed minutes also mentioned the risks brought by AI industry debt and complex financing. Once tech stock valuations adjust and risk appetite declines, it is likely to further impact Bitcoin. Furthermore, the Japanese market has brought another layer of concern. On November 18, the average winning bid yield for Japanese 20-year government bonds rose to 3.756%, reflecting a weakening demand for long-term government bonds and causing the market to refocus on changes in Japan's financing environment. In the past, some investors would borrow low-cost Japanese yen to buy risky assets like Bitcoin. Once yen financing costs rise, or the yen continues to appreciate, these carry trades may be forced to close, leading to new selling pressure. Of course, Bitcoin itself isn't without buying interest. Glassnode data shows that during the weekend sell-off, approximately 66,000 BTC entered the $62,000 to $66,000 cost range for short-term holders. This range has now become an important support area. Furthermore, the bid depth near the spot price on leading exchanges is about 2.3 times that of the sell orders, indicating that some funds are trying to absorb the selling pressure. However, orders do not equal actual transactions, and whether the buying momentum can be sustained remains to be seen. Ultimately, the biggest problem facing this rebound is not whether there is enough capital to buy at the bottom, but whether this buying power can offset the pressure from the macroeconomic environment. Therefore, while holding above $60,000 is important, what's more crucial than price is whether market confidence can be restored. What Bitcoin truly needs to prove next is whether it can still attract sufficient real buying interest given the current easing of global liquidity. As we've seen, the Nasdaq has rebounded somewhat in overnight trading; let's see if this can bring in a wave of effective capital. After all, even if AI stocks have peaked in the short term, there are still growth expectations. Unless even profit expectations start to decline, that would be another piece of bad news, and that will depend on the next quarter's earnings reports.

data.title: The all-new Gemini 4 Neon is now available, boasting a massive Opus 5.5.
data.description:
Another update! Another update! The AI ​​community is practically celebrating the New Year every day!

Just now, the fourth member of the Google Gemini 4 family, Neon, officially launched.

Hassabis personally posted the official announcement, calling it "the pinnacle of alchemy."

It prioritizes fast inference, specifically designed for high-frequency, complex software engineering, knowledge analysis, and long-term scientific research tasks. The overall cost of running a task on Neon is not only 50% to 80% lower than top-tier flagship processors like Claude and GPT, but its performance is also uncompromising. Google officially compared Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol side-by-side. In 19 tests, Neon achieved the highest score in 16!

Let's highlight the key features of this release.

  • Intelligence surpasses flagship：AA Intelligence Index of 61 points, ranking third globally, one point higher than its own flagship Carbon.

    ：AA Intelligence Index of 61 points, ranking third globally, one point higher than its own flagship Carbon.

    ：AA Intelligence Index of 61 points, ranking third globally, one point higher than its own flagship Carbon.

    ：AA Intelligence Index of 61 points, ranking third globally, one point higher than its own flagship Carbon.

    **Programming Agent #1:** AA Programming Agent tops the leaderboard with a score of 58.6, costing just over half the price of Claude Opus 5.5 to complete a task. **Nearly Twice as Fast:** Outputs approximately 110 tokens per second, compared to Carbon's 57. Price: $3 per million token input, $15 per million token output, with a cache hit costing only $0.15, and a context of 1 million tokens. Can be the Commander: In Google's Agent programming platform Antigravity, Neon can command a group of Hydrogen sub-Agents to work in parallel.

Turing's study is resurrected as it is,500,000 table formula drawing 3D 

Swarm and Super-agent manage two layers of work

Neon's Swarm collaboration with a group of Hydrogens seems similar at first glance to DeepSeek's recently proposed Super-agent, but they actually manage different layers of work.

What are they respectively

  • Swarm:A division of labor scheme within a task.

    Neon is responsible for planning, judgment, and acceptance, while Hydrogen is responsible for writing code, modifying files, and running tests. The goal is to do a good job quickly and efficiently. Super-agent: A persistent, online Agent system that manages multiple tasks simultaneously. The Router is responsible for receiving messages, associating tasks, and dispatching work. Multiple Workers each do their own thing, aiming to continuously monitor multiple tasks in parallel without requiring users to monitor each session individually. Separate Coordination and Execution: One layer is responsible for scheduling, and the other layer is responsible for execution. Both have feedback loops: When problems are encountered during execution, they are reported, adjustments are made, and then progress continues. Both save time for users: Users don't need to personally arrange every step or chase after every executor. What's the difference? The scope of management: Swarm manages how tasks are divided within a single task, while Super-agent manages how multiple tasks are scheduled and continuously monitored. Who does the brainwork: Neon needs to thoroughly understand the task and personally devise solutions; the Super-agent Router should primarily handle association and dispatch, leaving complex reasoning to the Worker. Where to put the strong model: Google places the powerful Neon at the top layer, paired with the fast Hydrogen; DeepSeek suggests the opposite: the Router can be lighter, while the Worker needs a stronger model. Model Binding: Swarm uses a fixed set of models; Super-agent is a system design that allows different models to be assigned to different roles, or the same model to be used for all roles. The Agent era's super ace, Google's four consecutive releases in seven weeks. The Agent era was about who could break down a major task, assign it, and inspect it themselves, completing it in one go. Today, Google has given the top command position to a mid-tier team, with the flagship Carbon only appearing for the most difficult tasks. This hit Claude squarely. Agents that write code and perform long-term tasks have always been Claude's strongest asset, but Fable 5.2, released only nine days ago, was overtaken by Neon on the programming agent leaderboard. More than the narrow margin, Google's rapid pace is Claude's real problem. Since November 10th, Google has released three Gemini 4 models. Google's explanation for this rapid pace is RSI (Resource Injection). Google co-founder Brin stated in October that Google was on the "RSI treadmill," with researchers working alongside models to build the next generation of models. If Google's internal RSI system truly gets going, with each generation of models being built faster than the last, the trump card of the super-intelligent era will fall into Gemini's hands. Now, the pressure is on Claude and GPT.

data.title: Has the selling pressure been exhausted? Bitcoin selling momentum observation
data.description:
Author: Anthony Pompliano, Founder and CEO of Pomp Investments; Translated by: Shaw, Jinse Finance

One ​​of Bitcoin's major advantages is that it has become one of the most transparent assets globally. Relying on available on-chain data and the various data platforms built up in recent years, analysts can conduct real-time assessments of Bitcoin, something most traditional assets cannot do.

For investors planning to buy Bitcoin on dips, several positive market signals have emerged.

First, Matthew Sigel of VanEck points out: When Bitcoin's RSI falls to 24, there is almost no risk of loss over the next 12 months.

This signal has only appeared once in Bitcoin's history, followed by a year of price decline. Charles Edwards' data shows that the long-term holder inflation rate has finally reached a key level, the last time it appeared was at the bottom of the 2022 bear market. The long-term holder inflation indicator measures the net buying or selling behavior of investors holding positions for ≥155 days and is a high-quality signal for judging the clearing of panic selling at the market bottom.

Just as these signals were emerging simultaneously, Wall Street institutions were buying Bitcoin heavily in the third quarter. Bitcoin platform River stated that these institutions will continue to increase their Bitcoin positions amidst the continued volatility in the stock market.

... The participation of institutional funds is a key reason why the volatility of this Bitcoin bear market is lower than in previous bear markets. Strive's Joe Burnett points out: "Bitcoin has retraced 50% from its high, but its one-year volatility has consistently remained below 47% throughout this bear market. In the 2022 bear market, volatility never fell below 65%; in the 2018 bear market, volatility never fell below 86%. Bitcoin's bear market is becoming increasingly stable." This is exactly the phenomenon we're happy to see: As more institutions enter the market to buy, Bitcoin's downside volatility continues to decrease. This might diminish some of the asymmetric advantage of upward returns, but in the long run, the amount of capital available to allocate to this asset will increase significantly. Furthermore, various indicators are signaling a weakening of selling momentum, making the current price level a good entry point and suitable for further, phased accumulation of Bitcoin. The above content is not financial advice. Everyone's situation is different. However, the better you understand market cycles, the more informed your decisions will be.

data.title: Coinbase AI Blocks $4.7M in Deepfake Crypto Scam
data.description:
A Deepfake Giveaway Targets Crypto Investors

Coinbase says its AI-powered fraud prevention systems blocked approximately US$4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers linked to a fraudulent livestream impersonating Elon Musk.

The scammers created a fake YouTube broadcast resembling Tesla's flying-car demonstration, featuring an AI-generated Musk, cryptocurrency wallet addresses and QR codes. Viewers were promised that any cryptocurrency they sent would be returned at double the amount, a familiar giveaway scam tactic designed to encourage quick transfers.

The livestream reportedly attracted more than 500,000 viewers. Within approximately two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers attempted to send millions of dollars to the scammer-controlled wallets.

AI Intervenes Before Funds Leave Accounts

Coinbase reported that its AI-powered defences prevented approximately 91% of the attempted transfers, totalling US$4.7 million, without human intervention.

Its system uses machine-learning models to identify suspicious outgoing transactions based on indicators such as giveaway patterns, impersonation of well-known brands and newly created wallet addresses.

When a transfer is flagged, an AI scam-prevention agent engages the customer in a conversation, explaining the warning signs and questioning the legitimacy of the offer. The objective is to interrupt the decision-making process before the victim completes an irreversible transaction.

Coinbase said the AI agent had not previously encountered this specific scam but recognised its underlying patterns, including promises of multiplied funds, event-driven urgency and irreversible payments.

The Challenge of Scams Without Account Compromise

Unlike conventional cyberattacks involving stolen passwords, account takeovers or phishing credentials, this incident involved customers authorising transfers themselves.

The victims were logged into their legitimate accounts and willingly initiated transactions because they believed the livestream was genuine. Traditional fraud detection systems designed primarily to identify unauthorised account access may struggle to recognise when a legitimate user is being manipulated.

This creates a different security problem: protecting users from fraudulent decisions made under deception rather than from unauthorised access alone.

AI-assisted transaction analysis and real-time customer intervention may help exchanges detect contextual warning signs that conventional rule-based systems overlook.

Deepfakes Make Financial Fraud More Convincing

Generative AI has made it easier for scammers to produce convincing videos, voice recordings and livestreams impersonating public figures, executives and trusted organisations.

Celebrity impersonation scams are particularly effective in the cryptocurrency sector because audiences may associate prominent technology personalities with digital assets, investment opportunities and new financial products.

By combining fabricated video, familiar branding, live-event timing and promises of guaranteed returns, scammers can create an illusion of legitimacy while pressuring victims to act quickly.

The growing accessibility of deepfake technology means such campaigns can be repeatedly recreated, translated and distributed across different platforms with relatively little effort.

What Organisations and Users Should Learn

The incident highlights several priorities for cryptocurrency platforms and their customers:

  • Context-aware fraud detection: Monitor not only account access but also the intent and circumstances surrounding transactions.
  • Real-time intervention: Introduce timely warnings and friction when users appear to be sending funds to suspicious addresses.
  • Adaptive AI defences: Identify emerging scam patterns that may not match previously known fraud signatures.
  • Public awareness: Educate customers that legitimate giveaways do not require sending cryptocurrency first to receive a larger amount in return.
  • Independent verification: Confirm promotions through official websites and verified channels rather than livestream QR codes or wallet addresses.

Conclusion: AI Is Becoming Both the Scam and the Safeguard

The Coinbase incident illustrates the evolving relationship between AI-driven fraud and AI-powered defence. Deepfake technology enables scammers to create increasingly persuasive financial deception, while automated security agents can analyse suspicious transactions and intervene before funds are lost.

Although Coinbase's reported intervention demonstrates the potential of AI to reduce fraud at scale, no automated system can eliminate every scam or guarantee that suspicious transfers will always be stopped.

As digital financial fraud becomes more sophisticated, the combination of intelligent transaction monitoring, timely intervention and informed users will be essential in protecting cryptocurrency ecosystems.

Sources:

  • The Block — Coinbase AI defense blocks $4.7M from being sent to deepfake Elon Musk scam, 17 November 2026.

  • Coinbase — Official reporting on AI-powered scam prevention, 17 November 2026.
